purpose: Human-reviewable plan consumed by Scripts/release_transit_bridge.py: place and configure ONE AMikdashTransitBoardingBridge in the combined Walkthrough map, wired to the single placed AMikdashTransit and AMikdashCrowdField. Nothing here is a claim of visual or runtime acceptance: the bridge's own arithmetic is covered by Plugins/MikdashRuntime/Tests/BoardingBridgeMathTest.cpp and its behaviour in a world needs PIE.
actorLocationNote: Every figure transform the bridge writes is world space; the actor transform is applied to nothing and is pinned at the origin.

coordinatorGuard.note: AMikdashTransitCrowdCoordinator is the earlier transfer renderer bound to OnPassengerExchange. Both running would animate every exchange twice, so placement is refused while a coordinator with activate_on_begin_play is present, and the bridge itself refuses to start in that case (b_refuse_if_coordinator_active).

mountFocusNote: Legacy 50 cm main map: the Temple stands at the origin and photographers face it. In the isolated 48 cm candidate the sanctuary is at a different world position; this spec targets the main map only and the guard refuses any other map.

invariants.poolCoversCap: max_figures >= max_concurrent_groups * max_people_per_group, so the cap, not the pool, is what bounds a busy moment.
invariants.fanClearance: 0.34 * dispersal_min_cm >= door_clearance_cm and 0.34 * photo_spot_min_cm >= door_clearance_cm (cos 70 degrees = 0.342).

routesNote: Read offline only to report, per stop, the largest boarding request the transit layer can raise (boardingMaxPeople x the transit density multiplier, capped at 8x) against what the bridge will animate with the default dwell; the offline check refuses a spec whose pool cannot hold max_concurrent_groups groups of max_people_per_group.
scope: Placement, checkpoint, save, reopen and numeric readback of one bridge actor. NOT visual acceptance, NOT proof that any figure appears: that needs a real-RHI PIE run with the transit actor active, read through GetBridgeSummary().
